summary: We are testing whether a specific tree decomposition algorithm (L/R leaf-tracking) can solve problem #22 — constructing a new tree with bags of size ≤4 and ≤4N vertices that covers all tree and ring edges while maintaining the running intersection ("revolutionary set") property. One experiment arm will implement this algorithm in C++ and measure the judge score (0–100).
key_points: Problem #22 asks us to build a tree decomposition of an 'outerplanar' graph (original tree + leaf ring road) with bag size ≤4 and at most 4N bags, satisfying a connectivity/running-intersection property for each original vertex.

The single arm (h-main) implements a DFS-based algorithm that computes leftmost/rightmost leaves L[u], R[u] for each node, then builds three types of bags per internal node (H, S, Lnk) connected in a spine structure, covering all tree edges and ring edges with bags of size exactly 4.

Confirmation criterion: judge score = 100 (valid decomposition on all test cases). Refutation: score < 100, which would indicate either a violated running-intersection property, an uncovered edge, a bag size exceeding 4, or K > 4N — diagnostics in the hypothesis point to specific failure modes to check.
This is iteration 1 with a single mechanism arm; no ablation is needed because the score is expected to be binary (fully correct or not). The judge call takes ~30–60 seconds and will be run once.
